title: feat(chatbot): draw verified record citations as chips that open the cited section
body:
Fixes #37365
Clause-②: yes (a new reserved URL parameter `section`)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：使用应用内 AI 的用户，在回答下方看到“引自记录”的引用条（每条显示摘句）；点一条就打开那条记录，并滚到被引的那一节、高亮标出。
- 为什么做：记录 AI 问询专题的第 10b 行，让用户能从 AI 回答一键跳回原文核对。
- 出错会怎样：引用条不显示或跳到记录顶部，记录本身与数据不受影响；撤回本次合并即可恢复原样。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

Governing text: ADR-0160 D9 as amended by #37363; ruling 7177410380 on #37144 (Q1 A: draw the persisted, already-verified list, never re-verify; Q3 A: a related-row quote opens the root record).

- **Lift** (`plugin-chatbot/src/mapMessages.ts`): `extractRecordCitations(parts)` reads the last `data-record-citations` part (`RECORD_CITATIONS_PART_TYPE`) through the spec's `RecordCitationsSchema`. A part the schema refuses, or an empty list, is no list (the `detectAnswerSource` precedent). `uiMessageToChatMessage` carries it as `recordCitations`; `chatMessageAdapter.ts` names the new render-only key.
- **Chips** (`plugin-chatbot/src/RecordCitations.tsx`, new; drawn in `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` beside `AnswerSourceBlock`): one chip per citation showing the quote. A click calls `onOpenRecord({ objectName: object, recordId: id, anchor })`; `onOpenRecord`'s argument gains an optional `anchor`. Nothing is fetched or verified on display.
- **Open** (`app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx`): `openRecord` takes the optional `anchor` and navigates to `recordOpenTarget(app, …)` = `/apps/APP/OBJ/record/ID?section=ANCHOR`. The dock and the `/ai` page both draw this `ChatPane`.
- **Param** (`app-shell/src/urlParams.ts`): `RECORD_SECTION_PARAM = 'section'`, in `RESERVED_URL_PARAMS` and the param table. `RECORD_SECTION_OPENED_STATE` is a history-state key, not a URL parameter (the `RECORD_COMMENTS_PUSHED_STATE` precedent).
- **Record page** (`app-shell/src/views/recordSectionAnchor.ts`, new; wired in `RecordDetailView.tsx`): once the record is held, the spec's `headingsOf` runs on each long-text field (`markdown`, `html`/`richtext`, `textarea`) in field order; the first whose outline issues the anchor is the body. The heading element is found in that field's drawn face and scrolled to and marked (the linked-comment marking). The match is trusted only when the face draws exactly as many headings of that title as the outline lists. A `textarea` body, a heading that is not drawn within 4 s, a count that differs, or a heading with no letter or digit scrolls to the field. A stale anchor opens the top. The cleanup takes the mark off, so opening another section moves the mark. Each chip click carries a fresh history-state value (`RECORD_SECTION_OPENED_STATE`), so the same chip clicked again opens its section again; a navigation that keeps the state, such as a tab switch, does not.
- **Field marker** (`plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx`): each detail row carries `data-detail-field={field.name}`, which is how the page finds a field. One attribute, no behaviour change.
- **i18n**: `chatbot.recordCitations.title` in all 11 `ui/packages/i18n` locales.
- Docs: `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`, `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/README.md`; changeset `.changeset/37365-record-citation-chips.md` (patch, four `@object-ui/*` packages).

Read first, by risk:
1. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/recordSectionAnchor.ts`: `locateSection` (how a drawn heading is matched) and `focusRecordSection` (observer and settle timer).
2. `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/mapMessages.ts`: `extractRecordCitations` (the parse gate).
3. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`: the effect beside `holdsRouteRecord`.

## Tests

## Acceptance notes

- **Which field is the body.** The URL carries only `section`, so the page cannot read the citation's `context` pack. It runs `headingsOf` on every long-text field the record holds (`markdown`, `html`, `richtext`, `textarea`), in field order, and the first whose outline issues the anchor is the body. When the pack's body field holds the anchor, the result is the same. Another long-text field earlier in the field order that has a heading with the same anchor would be opened instead. The alternative, reading the pack's `body.field`, would need `context` on the URL as well; it was not taken.
- **A2 (measured: holds only in part).** The drawn face shows headings that `headingsOf` does not list: setext headings, an empty `#`, headings inside a quote or a list, an indented ATX heading, and empty `h1`-`h6` in html. The outline also lists headings the face does not draw, such as a `#` line inside a raw HTML block or a four-backtick fence. With a bare Nth-element rule, each of these shifts every later heading. The rule taken (`locateSection`) has two parts. First, among the field's drawn heading elements, it picks those whose letters and digits read the same as the outline's heading and indexes them by the outline's repeat count. Second, it trusts that index only when the face draws exactly as many headings of that reading as the outline lists. Otherwise it opens the field, and it also opens the field for a heading with no letter or digit. So a differing heading of another title shifts nothing. A same-titled one, or a listed one the face does not draw, opens the field rather than a heading that may be another. A heading whose raw text carries letters the face does not draw (a link's URL) reads differently and opens at the field too. Two headings that normalise alike (`C` and `C++`) are told apart by order, which both sides share.
- **Moving the mark (round 2).** The focus cleanup takes the attribute and only the classes the mark added. A second citation on the open record, or the record left, leaves no stale mark. The chat opener puts a fresh `RECORD_SECTION_OPENED_STATE` value on each chip click, and the record page keys the focus on record, anchor and that value. So the same chip clicked again (same URL) scrolls and marks again. The tab and comment writers replace the URL keeping `location.state`, so they do not re-scroll.
- **Files beyond the claim's surface.** (1) `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx` gets one `data-detail-field` attribute on each detail row. Without it the page has no way to find a field, so the textarea and not-drawn cases could not open at the field. (2) `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chatMessageAdapter.ts` gets one key on `RuntimeOnlyMessageKeys`, the declared place for a new render-only message key. (3) The new helper `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/recordSectionAnchor.ts`. (4) The chatbot docs page and README. overlap-check is clean against `origin/main` and against #37436, which shares `DetailSection.tsx` and the 11 locale files (disjoint hunks), and #37422, which shares the 11 locale files.
- **Not covered: a reload.** The chips are drawn from the live stream. When the `/ai` page rebuilds history, it drops any `data-*` part other than charts: `hydratedMessagesToChatMessages`, then `useObjectChat`'s `initialMessages` rebuild, then the browser display cache (`sanitizeChatMessagesForCache`). So a persisted citation list does not come back after a reload yet; #37487 carries it. Nothing on `main` emits the part before cloud 10c. The changeset and both doc pages say so: the console draws a verified citations part when a live answer carries one.
- Clause-②: yes because a new console URL parameter is reserved. `onOpenRecord`'s argument gains an optional member (widening). No spec file changed.

## Verification

- Browser: **NOT MEASURED** here. The seat carries it on #37487's acceptance: scroll under the sticky chrome, ring visibility, the lazy face against the 4 s settle, the phone row, and `html`/`richtext` bodies. In its place, `RecordDetailView.citedSection-37365.test.tsx` renders the real record page with the real markdown face.
- Two-minute check: in the console, ask the assistant something an answer with a `data-record-citations` part covers (cloud 10c). Click a chip. Expected: the address is `/apps/APP/OBJ/record/ID?section=ANCHOR`, the cited heading is scrolled into view with the accent ring, and an edited-away heading opens the record at its top.
